Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Writ Petition No.11787 of 2023
Order:

(Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice K.Lakshman) Heard Sri Pothamshetti Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Mujeeb Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General.

2. This writ petition is filed challenging the detention order No.139/PDC/KNR/2023, dated 06.01.2023, confirmed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.360, General Administration (Spl-Law &
Order) Department, dated 08.03.2023 as illegal and arbitrary.
Petitioner herein is the wife of the detenu i.e., Bathini Thirupathi has filed this writ petition.
3. Perusal of record would reveal that the detenu, the petitioner's husband is a delivery boy in Samruddi Indane Gas Agency, Waddepalli, Hanmankonda.
Two crimes were registered against him.

Crime No.222 of 2022 of P.S. Manakondur was registered against the KL,J & PSS,J W.P.
No.11787_2023 detenu on 09.10.2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 457, 380 of IPC and Section 25(1)(a) of Arms Act.
The allegations against the detenu are that he has committing theft of 140 full and 140 empty gas cylinders from gas godown of the said firm.
The aforesaid case was registered on the complaint lodged by the Managing Partner of the aforesaid firm.

4. Crime No.293 of 2022 was registered by Karimnagar I Town Police Station against the detenu on 09.11.2022 on the complaint lodged by Managing Partner of the aforesaid firm for the offences punishable under Sections 452, 392 and 307 of IPC and Section 25(1)(a) of Arms Act.
The allegation against the detenu in the said complaint was extortion of money i.e., Rs.34,875/- by showing fire arms.

5. According to learned Special Government Pleader, the Investigating Officer in both the crimes have already completed investigation and filed charge sheets against the detenu and the same were taken on file and assigned calendar case numbers which are pending before the trial Court.
The allegations leveled against the detenu are serious, disturbed the public order.

Considering the nature KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 of offences, the manner in which, they were committed by the detenu, material on record, respondent No.2 passed detention order and confirmed by respondent Smt. Bathini Chitrakala vs The State Of Telangana on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164436788/
1 No.1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no irregularity.

6. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Apex Court held as under:
"...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some?

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.

A District Magistrate is entitled to take action under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under . (1966) 1 SCR 709 KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 ordinary circumstances.

It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.

It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."
7.

In Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana2, the Apex Court held as under:
13.

entities.text: Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There can be no doubt that for 'public order' to be disturbed, there must in turn be public disorder.

Mere contravention of law such as indulging in cheating or criminal breach of trust certainly affects 'law and order' but before it can be said to affect 'public order', it must affect the community or the public at large."

"24. On the facts of this case, as has been pointed out by us, it is clear that at the highest, a possible apprehension of breach of law and order can be said to be made out if it is apprehended that the Detenu, if set free, will continue to cheat gullible persons.
This may be a good ground to appeal against the bail orders granted and/or to cancel bail but certainly cannot provide the springboard to move under a preventive detention statute.
We, therefore, quash the detention order on this ground.
Consequently, it is unnecessary to go into any of .

(2021) 9 SCC 415 KL,J &
PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 the other grounds argued by the learned counsel on Smt. Bathini Chitrakala vs The State Of Telangana on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164436788/
2 behalf of the Petitioner.

entities.text: Smt. Bathini Chitrakala vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The impugned judgment is set aside and the Detenu is ordered to be freed forthwith.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed."
8.

In Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana3, the Apex Court held that a mere apprehension of a breach of law and order is not sufficient to meet the standard of adversely affecting the "maintenance of public order".

entities.text: Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Referring to the principle laid down by it in Ram Manohar Lohia3 and Banka Sneha Sheela5, the distinction between a disturbance to law and order and a disturbance to public order was discussed.

It was observed by the Apex Court that for the last five years, the Apex Court has quashed over five detention orders under the Telangana Act of 1986 for inter alia incorrectly applying the standard for maintenance of public order and relying on stale materials while passing the orders of detention.
At least ten detention orders under the Telangana Act of 1986 have been set aside by the Apex Court in the last one year itself.
These numbers evince a callous exercise of the exceptional power of preventive detention by the detaining authorities and the respondent - State.
Therefore, the Apex Court directed the respondents therein to take stock of .

2022 SCC OnLine SC 424 KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 challenges to detention orders pending before the Advisory Board, High Court and the Apex Court and evaluate the fairness of the detention order against lawful standards.

entities.text: 2022 SCC OnLine SC 424 KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 challenges
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similar view was reiterated by Apex Court in Shaik Nazneen v. The State of Telangana4.
9.

entities.text: Shaik Nazneen v. The State of Telangana4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judgment in Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana (2 Supra), was delivered on 04.04.2022.

entities.text: Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana (2 Supra)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Even then, the respondents have passed order of detention in the present writ petition on 06.01.2023.
10.
As discussed in the present case, in both the aforesaid crimes, detenu was released on bail.
Perusal of record would reveal that there are disputes between the Managing Partner of the aforesaid firm and the detenu, delivery boy with regard to supply of gas cylinders.
The aforesaid allegations are between the Managing Partner and the detenu and they are nothing to do with the public order.
There is disturbance to public order.
Respondent authorities have to try the detenu for the offences punishable under the aforesaid provisions of IPC as well as Arms Act.
2022 LiveLaw (SC) 559 KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 11.
Perusal of record would also reveal that respondent authorities have not opposed the bail application of the detenu.
They have not filed any application seeking cancellation of the bail granted to the detenu in the 1st crime on the ground that he has involved in 2nd crime committed similar offences.

Therefore, respondents cannot invoke the procedure laid down under the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-Leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas,
Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders,
Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short 'the Act, 1986').

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court and Division Bench of this Court time and again held that the respondent authorities shall invoke the provisions of the Act 1986 in rarest of the rare case there too, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences.
They have drawn a distinction between public order and law and order
In the KL,J & PSS,J W.P. No.11787_2023 present case, there is no disturbance to public order as alleged by respondent No.2 in the detention order.
There is consideration of the said aspects by respondent No.1 while confirming the detention order.

13. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this writ petition is allowed, the impugned detention order,
dated 06.01.2023 approved by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.360, General Administration (Spl-Law & Order) Department, dated 08.03.2023 are hereby set aside.
The respondents are directed to set the detenue namely Bathini Thirupathi S/o.

Late Rajaiah, Age: 41 years, R/o.
H.No.5-211, Nagunur (V), Karimnagar Mandal and District, who is now detained in Central Prison,
Cherlapally, Medchal-Malkajgiri District, free forthwith, if he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
There shall be no order as to costs.
14. As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
_ _ _ K. LAKSHMAN, J ____________________ P. SREE SUDHA, J June 12, 2023
Note: Issue CC forthwith.
